cues.en: This episode is sponsored by Crunchyroll. Today on Space Time, we're going to talk about time space, or the strange switching in the roles of space and time that occurs in the mathematics when we drop below the event horizon of a black hole. cues.en: or doesn't correspond to real, timey, wimey weirdness. We've been working up to this one, so you might want to hit pause and check out these episodes if you think you need some more background. OK? Let's get started. First, we'll think about what the flow of time looks like without black holes or even spacetime curvature. When we talked about the geometry of causality, we saw that this quantity that we call the spacetime interval governs the flow of cause and effect.
cues.zh: 还是并不对应于真实的、时间上的、奇异的怪事。我们一直在为这个话题做准备，所以如果你想了解更多背景，不妨暂停一下，看看这些往期节目。好了，我们开始吧。首先，我们思考一下没有黑洞、甚至没有时空曲率时，时间的流动是什么样子。当我们讨论因果性的几何时，我们看到这个被称为时空间隔的量支配着因果的流动。

cues.en: the only reliable ordering of events in a relative universe. I'm going to show you the math one more time, and then we'll get back to doing all of this graphically. The spacetime interval is defined like this for boring old flat or Minkowski space. Different observers may report that two events are separated by different distances, delta x, and by different amounts of time, delta t. However, all observers record the same spacetime interval.
cues.zh: 这是在相对宇宙中唯一可靠的事件排序方式。我再给大家展示一次数学推导，然后我们回到用图形来做这些。时空间隔在无聊的旧平坦空间或闵可夫斯基空间中是这样定义的。不同观察者可能报告两个事件相隔不同的距离delta x，以及不同的时间量delta t。然而，所有观察者记录到的时空间隔是相同的。

cues.en: If one event causes a second event, the spacetime interval must be 0 or negative. That just means that a light-speed causal link may have traveled between them. You could say that an object at a given spacetime instant is caused by whatever version of itself existed an instant earlier. So world lines of objects have decreasing spacetime intervals. In fact,
cues.zh: 如果一个事件导致第二个事件，时空间隔必须是0或负值。这只意味着它们之间可能有一条光速因果链连接。你可以说，一个物体在某个时空瞬间的状态，是由它前一个瞬间存在的版本所导致的。所以物体的世界线具有递减的时空间隔。事实上，

cues.en: Forward temporal evolution requires a negative spacetime interval. In flat spacetime, that negative sign in front of the delta t drives that forward evolution. This makes t the time-like coordinate, while x is the spacelike coordinate. For causality to be maintained, the time-like coordinate must always increase. Reversing causality means flipping the sign of the spacetime interval.
cues.zh: 向前的时间演化需要负的时空间隔。在平坦时空中，delta t前面的负号驱动了这种向前演化。这使得t成为类时坐标，而x是类空坐标。为了维持因果性，类时坐标必须始终增加。逆转因果性意味着翻转时空间隔的符号。

cues.en: In our episode on superluminal time travel, we saw that in flat space, this means traveling faster than light, which is, of course, impossible. But if we introduce a black hole, we now have a second way to flip the side of the spacetime interval. We're going to see how this changes the behavior of time in very strange ways. Add a non-rotating, uncharged black hole, and the spacetime interval becomes this.
cues.zh: 在我们关于超光速时间旅行的那期节目中，我们看到在平坦空间中，这意味着超光速旅行，这当然是不可能的。但如果我们引入一个黑洞，我们现在就有了第二种翻转时空区间一侧的方法。我们将看到这如何以非常奇怪的方式改变时间的行为。添加一个不旋转、不带电的黑洞，时空区间就变成了这样。

cues.en: This comes from Carl Schwarzschild's solution to the Einstein field equations, the very first accurate description of a black hole. I've left out a few terms. This equation assumes no orbital motion, only motion towards or away from the center of the black hole, which is a distance r away. That rs is the Schwarzschild radius, the radius of the event horizon. Very far from the event horizon,
cues.zh: 这来自卡尔·史瓦西对爱因斯坦场方程的解，这是对黑洞的第一个精确描述。我略去了几个项。这个方程假设没有轨道运动，只有朝向或远离黑洞中心的运动，距离为r。那个rs是史瓦西半径，即事件视界的半径。在离事件视界非常远的地方，

cues.en: The Schwarzschild interval becomes the good old Minkowski interval, and time and space are nicely separated. But if an object gets close to the event horizon, so r just a little bit bigger than rs, that stuff in the two brackets describes extreme warping of spacetime. But as long as you're outside the event horizon, time behaves itself, mostly.
cues.zh: 史瓦西区间变成了熟悉的闵可夫斯基区间，时间和空间很好地分开了。但如果一个物体靠近事件视界，所以r只比rs大一点点，那两个括号里的东西描述了时空的极端扭曲。但只要你还在事件视界外面，时间基本上还是守规矩的。

cues.en: A negative space-time interval still means causal movement, and the only way to break causality is still with faster than light travel. Things change radically below the event horizon when R gets smaller than RS. Then both of these brackets become negative. The entire delta R stuff is now negative, and the delta T stuff is positive. Below the event horizon, there is only one way to maintain the respectable causal progression.
cues.zh: 负的时空区间仍然意味着因果运动，而打破因果性的唯一方法仍然是超光速旅行。在事件视界以下，当R小于RS时，情况会发生根本性变化。然后这两个括号都变成负的。整个delta R部分现在是负的，而delta T部分是正的。在事件视界以下，只有一种方法可以维持体面的因果进程。

cues.en: expected of a well-mannered temporal entity, that's to fall inwards to have a non-zero delta r. As it happens, you don't have a choice. Space itself is falling inwards faster than the speed of light towards the central singularity. It carries you with it and drives your personal clock forward as it does so. In the mathematics, the coordinate r, which once represents a distance, now grants the negative sign needed to maintain your causal flow.
cues.zh: 作为一个有礼貌的时间实体，本该向内坠落，产生非零的delta r。但事实上，你别无选择。空间本身正以超光速向内坠向中心奇点。它裹挟着你一起坠落，同时推动你的个人时钟向前。在数学上，坐标r曾经代表距离，现在则提供了维持因果流动所需的负号。

cues.en: It becomes timelike. It's unidirectional. Meanwhile, the coordinate previously known as time, t, lost its negative sign and becomes spacelike. So it can be traversed in any direction or not traversed at all. But what does all of this time-space switching actually look like? Let's fall into the black hole one more time, now graphically instead of mathematically.
cues.zh: 它变成了类时的。它是单向的。与此同时，曾经被称为时间的坐标t失去了负号，变成了类空的。所以它可以朝任何方向穿越，或者根本不穿越。但所有这些时间-空间的转换到底长什么样？让我们再掉进黑洞一次，这次用图形而非数学来展示。

cues.en: Back out here in the regular universe, it's pretty obvious where the past and the future are. On our ever-popular space-time diagram, we see a sharp division between the two. Our past light cone encompasses all of space-time that could have influenced us, while our future light cone shows us the parts of the universe that we might ever hope to encounter or influence. Which direction is the future? Ahead, along our time axis,
cues.zh: 回到外面的常规宇宙，过去和未来的位置一目了然。在我们常用的时空图上，两者之间有明确的分界。我们的过去光锥包含了所有可能影响过我们的时空，而未来光锥则展示了我们可能遇到或影响到的宇宙部分。未来在哪个方向？在前方，沿着我们的时间轴，

cues.en: and at right angles to all of our space axes. Our future light cone stares fixedly forwards, encompassing all spatial directions equally. This is no longer true if we introduce gravity. Close to a massive object, your future is no longer at right angles to space. It becomes slightly tilted in the direction of that mass. Send out a burst of future-defining light rays, and they won't spread out evenly because they bend towards the gravitational field.
cues.zh: 并且与所有空间轴成直角。我们的未来光锥固定朝前，平等地涵盖所有空间方向。但引入引力后，这就不再成立了。靠近大质量物体时，你的未来不再与空间成直角。它会朝那个质量的方向微微倾斜。发出一束定义未来的光线，它们不会均匀散开，因为会朝引力场弯曲。

cues.en: As you approach the event horizon of a black hole, more and more light rays are turned towards the event horizon. Your future light cone and your time axis begin to blur together with the inward radial axis of the black hole. At this point, it's time we switch diagrams. Close to and within the black hole, the Penrose diagram is much more useful. It deals with the extreme stretching of space and time by compactifying lines of constant space or time
cues.zh: 当你接近黑洞的事件视界时，越来越多的光线转向事件视界。你的未来光锥和时间轴开始与黑洞的向内径向轴模糊在一起。此时，我们该换图了。在黑洞附近及内部，彭罗斯图要实用得多。它通过紧致化等空间线或等时间线来处理空间和时间的极端拉伸

cues.en: close to its boundaries. We talked about these diagrams previously, but an important thing to remember is that the lines of constant space and time are curved so that light cones remain upright, and light always travels at a 45 degree angle, even inside the black hole. This entire diagonal line represents the event horizon. Watch what happens to our view of the universe as we approach it.
cues.zh: 靠近其边界。我们之前讨论过这些图，但要记住的重要一点是，等空间线和等时间线是弯曲的，以使光锥保持竖直，光始终以45度角传播，即使在黑洞内部也是如此。整条对角线代表事件视界。看看当我们接近它时，我们对宇宙的视野会发生什么变化。

cues.en: Our entire future light cone encompasses more and more of the event horizon. That last tiny sliver is a narrowing window directly above that you could escape to at close to the speed of light. Meanwhile, our past light cone now encompasses light that has been struggling to escape from just above the event horizon since the distant past. But we still see nothing from below the horizon.
cues.zh: 我们的整个未来光锥涵盖了越来越多的事件视界。最后那一小条是正上方一个狭窄的窗口，你可以以接近光速的速度逃向那里。与此同时，我们的过去光锥现在涵盖了从遥远的过去就一直试图从事件视界正上方逃逸的光。但我们仍然看不到视界下方的任何东西。

cues.en: Yet, as soon as we pass the horizon, everything changes. The outside universe exits our future light cone, which now just contains the singularity. We also begin to encounter a new set of photons from the past. At the moment of crossing, light rays from the event horizon itself are suddenly visible. In fact, we plummet through a sea of light that is eternally climbing outwards, but getting nowhere.
cues.zh: 然而，一旦我们越过视界，一切都会改变。外部宇宙离开了我们的未来光锥，现在未来光锥只包含奇点。我们也开始遇到一组来自过去的新光子。在穿越的那一刻，来自事件视界本身的光线突然可见。事实上，我们跌入了一片永远向外攀爬却无处可去的光海之中。

cues.en: After that, we have access to the history of the interior of the black hole. As we fall with the faster-than-light flow of space time, we overtake light that is outward pointing. That light isn't actually making headway outwards. It's trying to swim upstream and failing against the faster-than-light cascade of space time. Some of this light might be from the collapsing surface of the star that first formed the black hole, emitted long before we entered the event horizon.
cues.zh: 这样我们就能获取黑洞内部的历史。随着我们跟随超光速的时空流坠落，我们会追上向外传播的光。那些光实际上并没有向外推进，它们试图逆流而上，但无法抵抗超光速的时空瀑布。其中一些光可能来自最初形成黑洞的恒星坍缩表面，这些光在我们进入事件视界之前很久就发出了。

cues.en: It appears to come from below us because it's trying to climb upwards. In fact, though, it was emitted at larger radio than wherever we encounter it. Also in our past light cone are light rays that are pointed inwards, some of them coming from the outside universe. This light overtakes us as we fall. This is light that entered the event horizon after we did and appears to reach us from above. We can try to move towards either source of light.
cues.zh: 它似乎来自我们下方，因为它试图向上攀升。但实际上，它是在比我们遇到它的位置更大的半径处发出的。同样在我们的过去光锥中的还有向内传播的光线，其中一些来自外部宇宙。这些光在我们下落时追上我们。这是在我们之后进入事件视界的光，似乎从上方到达我们这里。我们可以尝试朝任一光源移动。

cues.en: down towards light from the black hole's past or up towards light from the black hole's future. Those directions, those spatial freedoms, are now described by what was once the time coordinate. But it's no longer timelike. You can traverse it in either direction, making it spacelike. Doing so isn't actually traveling in time, even though there's a sense of past events in one direction, the collapsing star, and future events in the other, everything that fell into the black hole after us.
cues.zh: 向下朝黑洞过去的光，或向上朝黑洞未来的光。那些方向，那些空间自由度，现在由曾经的时间坐标来描述。但它不再是类时的。你可以朝任一方向穿越它，使其成为类空的。这样做实际上并不是在时间中旅行，尽管一个方向有过去事件的感觉——坍缩的恒星，另一个方向有未来事件——所有在我们之后落入黑洞的东西。

cues.en: But remember that our future light cone actually just points towards the singularity. If we try to accelerate in either direction up or down, we just quicken our demise. Best just to fall. It's the last mercy granted by the black hole. It transports us to our doom by the slowest path, unless we resist. Below the event horizon, there's still a sense of spatial upness and downness. However, the old radial dimension isn't space-like.
cues.zh: 但记住，我们的未来光锥其实只是指向奇点。如果我们试图向上或向下加速，只会加速自己的灭亡。最好就是坠落。这是黑洞给予的最后慈悲。它让我们以最慢的路径走向末日，除非我们抵抗。在事件视界之下，仍然有空间上的上下感。然而，旧的径向维度不再是类空的。

cues.en: It's timelike. Every photon that reaches us was emitted at some larger radius than wherever we encounter it. Even if it's old light struggling outwards, the past is radially outwards, and all possible future directions lead radially inwards in the same way that all world lines move towards the future in the outside universe. Time is layered radially, and R is timelike, unidirectional.
cues.zh: 它是类时的。每一个到达我们的光子，都是在比我们遇到它的地方更大的半径处发射的。即使是努力向外挣扎的古老光线，过去也是径向向外的，而所有可能的未来方向都径向向内，就像外部宇宙中所有世界线都走向未来一样。时间是径向分层的，而R是类时的、单向的。

cues.en: The singularity becomes a future time, not a central place. In fact, the Schwarzschild metric really gives two separate spacetime maps in a single equation, one for above and one for below the event horizon. The coordinates r and t play different roles in those regions. There are other coordinate systems in which that switch never happens, but this mysterious dimensional flip
cues.zh: 奇点变成了一个未来的时间，而不是一个中心位置。事实上，史瓦西度规在一个方程中确实给出了两个独立的时空图，一个用于事件视界之上，一个用于事件视界之下。坐标r和t在这些区域扮演不同的角色。还有其他坐标系，那种切换永远不会发生，但这个神秘的维度翻转

The systems that were tested use electron spins, which pull on each other to cause a cascading flow of flipping spins that cycles back and forth. Really, though, the term time crystal is just used to refer to anything that has
cues.zh: 你们中有些人不太确定究竟什么才算时间晶体。就目前而言，这个词的使用还相当宽泛。它指的是任何内部相互作用会导致其状态发生周期性改变、从一种状态转变为另一种再循环回来的量子系统。已测试的系统利用了电子自旋，自旋之间相互牵引，引起自旋翻转的级联流动并来回循环。不过说实话，“时间晶体”这个术语其实就是用来指代任何具有

cues.en: pattern of internal states that repeats over time. It doesn't also have to be a regular crystal that has a repeating spatial pattern. In fact, it typically won't be. Colin Brown asks if the spin flip oscillation is only dependent on the electromagnetic field oscillation. And he also asks why that's so special.
cues.zh: 随时间重复的内部状态模式的系统。它并不一定非要是那种具有空间重复模式的常规晶体。事实上，通常都不是。Colin Brown 问：自旋翻转振荡是否仅仅取决于电磁场振荡？他还问这到底有什么特别之处。

cues.en: Firstly, yeah, these time crystals oscillate at an integer multiple of the electromagnetic field frequency. So the time crystal oscillation and the EM field oscillation are in resonance. For every one, two, three, et cetera, cycles of the time crystal, the EM field gives a little push. It has to be an integer factor, because if the EM field were pushing halfway through the time crystal period, it would be pushing in the wrong direction. It's like when you're pushing a swing.
cues.zh: 首先，没错，这些时间晶体的振荡频率是电磁场频率的整数倍。因此时间晶体的振荡与电磁场振荡处于共振状态。时间晶体每完成一、二、三个等等周期，电磁场就会推它一把。它必须是整数倍关系，因为如果电磁场在时间晶体周期的半途发力，推的方向就反了。这就像是在推秋千一样。

cues.en: You don't need to push every time to keep it going, but you do need to push at the right time, or you'll slow it down. Colin and others also ask why this is so special. After all, lots of things oscillate, especially when you push them. So in Frank Wilczek's initial idea, his hypothetical time crystals didn't require any input energy to keep them oscillating.
cues.zh: 你不需要每次都推它来维持振荡，但必须在合适的时机推，否则反而会减慢它。Colin 和其他人也问，为什么这如此特别。毕竟很多东西都会振荡，尤其是当你推它们的时候。所以在 Frank Wilczek 最初的设想中，他假设的时间晶体不需要任何输入能量就能维持振荡。

cues.en: For Wilczek's time crystals, the oscillating state is an equilibrium state. And the oscillations were supposed to go on forever without any energy input. They will be special and weird, even if the original period was defined by an external EM field frequency. It's now been proved mathematically that time crystals can't exist in equilibrium. To keep them oscillating, you need to keep putting in energy.
cues.zh: 对 Wilczek 的时间晶体来说，振荡态是一种平衡态。而且这种振荡本应不需要任何能量输入就能永远持续下去。即便原始周期是由外部电磁场频率定义的，它们也会是特别而奇异的。现在数学上已经证明，时间晶体不可能在平衡态下存在。要让它们持续振荡，你就必须不断输入能量。

cues.en: However, the experimental results are still exciting because these systems did develop their own internal oscillations that resisted changes from the outside forcing EM field oscillation. So the oscillations were, in a sense, fundamental, just not sustainable. Is this more interesting than, say, a swinging pendulum? Well, pendulums are pretty cool, so I don't know. They're a new type of oscillating system that could have their own uses.
cues.zh: 不过，实验结果仍然令人兴奋，因为这些系统确实发展出了自己的内部振荡，并且抵抗了外部强迫电磁场振荡带来的变化。所以从某种意义上说，这些振荡是基本的，只是不可持续。这比，比如说，摆动的钟摆更有趣吗？嗯，钟摆挺酷的，所以我不知道。它们是一种新型的振荡系统，可能有自己的用途。

cues.zh: 我想感谢 Dankulous Memelord，因为对我们来说，这促发了一场关于本集可理解性的有益讨论。我们一直在关注反馈，以提高节目的清晰度，但这里值得说明的是，我们在时空主题上的目标与大多数科学媒体略有不同。我们希望提供一座通向理解真正科学的桥梁，并且比入门水平走得稍远一些。

cues.en: And that's especially true of the Spacetime Journal Club.
